title: The C_st-conjecture for dagger varieties: the fundamental diagram and its qBC geometrization
summary: Plan the analytic C_st comparison for smooth dagger varieties using the natural fundamental square, its finite bundle-cohomology obstructions and qBC filtration. Prove the equivalence with acyclicity, curvature and height for small varieties, the product/algebraic/almost-proper cases and proper-times-Stein limit case, followed by arithmetic and geometric recovery with their different information content. General smooth-dagger conjectures remain open.
readme:
# The C_st-conjecture for dagger varieties

The roadmap constructs the analytic fundamental diagram, measures its failure by cohomology of modified Fargues–Fontaine bundles, and proves comparison for the classes established by Colmez–Nizioł. For a small variety, the comparison is equivalent to acyclicity of the filtered Hyodo–Kato modules, nonpositive curvature of pro-étale cohomology, and the height identity. The arithmetic recovery theorem retains Frobenius, monodromy, Galois descent and the Hodge filtration. The geometric theorem recovers extended period modules from the natural Topological Vector Space functor.

This is a target-level formalisation plan. All six layers are **planned**, none is closed, and all mathematical implementation statuses are **unchecked**. Supplier contracts and proof gaps are part of the plan; they are not proved assumptions. The unrestricted smooth-dagger assertions in Conjectures 6.21 and 9.1, and universal small-variety acyclicity, remain open in the source. In particular, this roadmap does not claim that the general C_st-conjecture is proved.

The main source is Pierre Colmez and Wiesława Nizioł, *On the cohomology of p-adic analytic spaces, II: The C_st-conjecture*, Duke Mathematical Journal 174 (2025), 2203–2301, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1215/00127094-2024-0074). Locators below refer to the [61-page author manuscript CN5](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~wieslawa.niziol/CN5.pdf), compiled 24 November 2024, also checked against [arXiv v4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12785v4). The publisher text was not consulted. Source findings apply to those author/arXiv versions and require journal collation. Every statement here is formulated in the roadmap’s own words.

The [packet](../packets/CstConjectureForDaggerVarieties.json) records the dependency graph, source accounting and exact supplier requests. The [suggested Lean file](../suggested/CstConjectureForDaggerVarieties.lean) contains only checks expressible using existing pinned carriers. The reader is definitive: the missing dagger, modified-bundle, qBC and derived period objects are mathematical targets here, and are not replaced by abstract assertion parameters in Lean.

## Boundary and build order

Generic p-adic period rings, arithmetic filtered HN modules and the contravariant smooth-Galois period functors remain in PadicHodgeTheory R06.1–R06.2. The curve, vector bundles, classification, H⁰/H¹ and finite BC geometry remain in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB3. The current upstream AlgebraicVectorBundles and AdicSpaces documents were read, including their Suggested declarations; their constructions are imported, not re-planned. The new filtered-module object adds a C-valued lattice to those existing coefficients, and its bundle target constructs a particular modification rather than defining vector bundles again.

Dagger spaces and de Rham complexes remain in AdicSpacesPartII F1. The read finiteness/Künneth nodes there have discretely valued bases, and its resolution lemma has affinoid scope; the C-valued and proper-pair extensions used here are explicit gaps. CP.4 supplies its named algebraic comparison node, while its present scope does not supply model-free analytic HK/syntomic cohomology. General Pairs and qBC require the proposed vector-bundle Part II, whose stages are not yet defined. L0 supplies strict derived categories and qualified nonarchimedean duality. Its missing extension-duality hypotheses are retained, and no dependency on the unrelated noncommutative distribution-algebra Part II is introduced.

| Layer | Construction and exit criterion |
| --- | --- |
| CS.0 | C-lattice filtered modules, their modifications, acyclicity and bounded period Hom |
| CS.1 | Natural fundamental square, smallness, twists, proper/affinoid/Stein cases |
| CS.2 | Two bundle-cohomology failure terms, canonical qBC filtration, height and equivalent criteria |
| CS.3 | Products, algebraic analytifications, almost proper varieties and specified tube applications |
| CS.4 | Countable-exhaustion obstructions, proper-factor Künneth and proper-times-Stein comparison |
| CS.5 | Arithmetic and geometric recovery, with the stronger positive crystalline affinoid target separately qualified |

The splitting targets at the end of CS.2 form a separate branch. Their G-FA obligation is not used to prove geometric comparison or the main recovery theorems. CS.4 supplies a non-small comparison case; CS.5 does not infer a finite-rank recovery theorem for every space covered by CS.4.

## Conventions
1. p is prime. K is complete discretely valued of characteristic zero, with perfect countable residue field k of characteristic p; F=W(k)[1/p], Fⁿʳ is its maximal unramified extension inside K̄, and C is the completion of K̄. All analytic spaces are separated, taut and countable at infinity, as in §1.3.3, pp.7–8. A completed unramified coefficient field is used only where explicitly stated, never silently substituted for Fⁿʳ.

2. Nφ=pφN. Period tensors use diagonal operators; the imported B_st coordinate has N=−d/du. Every monodromy-untwisting formula must be adjusted to that sign. t has φ(t)=pt, and {−r} on HK multiplies φ by p⁻ʳ. Derived joint invariants, derived completed tensors, and natural locally convex Q_p topologies are part of the analytic input.

3. LH(C_Q_p) is the abelian left heart of the strict derived category of locally convex Q_p spaces. Tildes refer to left-heart cohomology; untilded groups are its classical part. VS is the source’s Vector Space functor category, TVS is the functor category of Definition 4.1: functors from sympathetic algebras into LH(C_Q_p), with uniform boundedness for algebra maps. Its morphisms are natural transformations. Evaluation at C is an ordinary locally convex space only for classical objects, and arbitrary continuous maps on C-points are not TVS morphisms. The change from VS to TVS needs its precise comparison theorem.

4. FilʳHⁱ means the image of Hⁱ(FʳRΓ) in Hⁱ(RΓ); Fʳⁱ denotes the former group itself. The kernel Aʳⁱ is often large and torsion. The square has u=(a,b) and v=(c,−d). Finite BC height is signed, qBC height extends it, and ht(Q_p)=1 while a reasonable torsion B_dR⁺-Pair has height zero.

5. For small X the induced F⁰ lattice in Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR) defines the filtered HK bundle. Smallness requires finite free B_dR⁺ cohomology in every degree. General Conjectures 6.21 and 9.1 are not promoted to unconditional theorem targets.


The natural TVS functor and its natural transformations are indispensable in the geometric theorem. In particular, Hom_TVS is not arbitrary continuous Q_p-linear Hom on a single cohomology group. Definition 4.1, p.21, specifies a functor on sympathetic algebras valued in the abelian left heart, with a boundedness condition on algebra maps; Definition 4.4, p.22, specifies qBCs. These imported definitions are included in G-QBC, not owned again here.

The pinned baseline is Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` and Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369`. The six exact baseline declarations read are BDeRhamPlus, BDeRham, CategoryTheory.BicartesianSq, Module.Free, Module.Finite and ModuleCat. The first two provide ring carriers under their stated completeness assumptions; they do not prove field/DVR properties. BicartesianSq is reused in the left heart, without a new square predicate. The library audit and direct pinned/current searches are recorded in the packet.


Each layer’s complete target statements occur in its description and in the definitive reader document. All layers are planned with the packet’s precise remaining supplier/proof obligations. General smooth-dagger conjectures stay open.

stages.title: Filtered period modules and modified bundles
stages.description:
Build the C-lattice version of filtered (φ,N)-modules on the imported coefficient objects; attach its modified bundle and acyclicity criteria. Prove bounded eigenspace generation and the three period-Hom comparisons needed for recovery. Generic arithmetic filtered HN theory and period functors are imported.

Targets:

**Filtered modules with a de Rham lattice** (definition). A filtered (φ,N)-module over C is a pair (M,L): M is finite dimensional over Fⁿʳ, φ is a bijective σ-semilinear map, N is Fⁿʳ-linear with Nφ=pφN, and L is a finite free B_dR⁺-submodule of M⊗B_dR spanning that module after inverting t. Morphisms are φ,N-equivariant maps carrying L into L′. The topology and period embeddings are the imported ones; C is not embedded canonically in B_dR⁺. Source: §5.3.1, p. 36.

**The bundle of a filtered module** (construction). Associate E(M,L) on the geometric Fargues–Fontaine curve by gluing the finite projective B_e-module (M⊗B_st)^{N=0,φ=1} away from ∞ to L at the completed local ring B_dR⁺, using their common B_dR-realization. Put V_st(M,L)=H⁰(E), equivalently the kernel of (M⊗B_st)^{N=0,φ=1}→(M⊗B_dR)/L. These are actual coherent bundles and section functors, not arbitrary modules labelled as bundles. Source: §5.3.1, p. 36.

**Weak admissibility and acyclicity over C** (definition). A pair (M,L) is weakly admissible when E(M,L) is semistable of slope zero; it is acyclic when every Harder–Narasimhan slope of E(M,L) is nonnegative. Both predicates hold for the zero object. With the imported convention for filtered objects over K, degree is t_H−t_N. Bundle slopes and BC curvature are distinct invariants. Source: Definition 5.13 and Remark 5.14(i), p. 36; §5.1.2, p. 32 (corrected sign).

**Cohomological criteria for acyclicity** (theorem). For a pair (M,L), acyclicity is equivalent to H¹(E(M,L))=0, to surjectivity of (M⊗B_st)^{N=0,φ=1}→(M⊗B_dR)/L, and to the existence of a sublattice L′⊆L for which (M,L′) is weakly admissible. Weak admissibility is equivalent to E≅O^rank(M), and also to finite Q_p-dimension of V_st together with exactness of its fundamental sequence. In that case V_st⊗B_st≅M⊗B_st and V_st⊗B_dR⁺≅L. Source: Remark 5.14(ii)–(iii), p. 36; Lemma 5.3, pp. 32–33.

**Bounded eigenspaces and period kernels** (definition). For r∈N, M with φ-slopes in [0,r], and a lattice L satisfying M⊗tʳB_dR⁺⊆tʳL⊆M⊗B_dR⁺, define the VS-valued X_stʳ(M)=(M⊗B_st⁺)^{N=0,φ=pʳ} and V_stʳ(M,L)=ker(X_stʳ(M)→(M⊗B_dR⁺)/tʳL). The bounded positive ring is essential: the displayed quotient map is not defined on the unrestricted B_st eigenspace. In the acyclic case this is a short exact sequence and V_stʳ=tʳV_st inside M⊗B_dR. More generally for k≥0 the t⁻ᵏB_st⁺-version maps onto (M⊗t⁻ᵏB_dR⁺)/tʳL iff the pair is acyclic, with the same kernel. Source: Remark 5.16, pp. 36–37; Proposition 5.20, p. 38 (positive-ring correction).

**Generation of the de Rham lattice** (theorem). If M has φ-slopes in [0,r], X_stʳ(M)(C) spans M⊗B_dR⁺ over B_dR⁺. This is generation by the bounded simultaneous N=0,φ=pʳ eigenspace, without a filtration or Galois hypothesis. Source: Lemma 5.17, p. 37.

**Period-valued Hom from an eigenspace** (theorem). For M with φ-slopes in [0,r], evaluation induces B_dR- and B_st-linear isomorphisms M∨⊗B_dR≅Hom_VS(X_stʳ(M), B_dR) and M∨⊗B_st≅Hom_VS(X_stʳ(M), B_st). Hom here means natural Q_p-linear Vector Space morphisms, not merely linear maps of C-points and not maps assumed period-linear. Source: Proposition 5.18 and Remark 5.19, pp. 37–38.

**Period-valued Hom from an acyclic kernel** (theorem). For an acyclic pair (M,L) with the bounds of CS.0/bounded-period-spaces, evaluation gives M∨⊗B_dR≅Hom_VS(V_stʳ(M,L), B_dR) and M∨⊗B_st≅Hom_VS(V_stʳ(M,L), B_st). These are module isomorphisms for the indicated period rings. Source: Proposition 5.20 and Remark 5.21, p. 38 (corrected lattice inclusion and Ext target).

**Period reconstruction modulo a power of t** (theorem). Under the same acyclicity and boundedness assumptions, for k≥2r the evaluation map M∨⊗(B_dR⁺/tᵏ)→Hom_VS(V_stʳ(M,L),B_dR⁺/tᵏ) has kernel killed by tʳ and cokernel killed by t²ʳ. In particular both are killed by t²ʳ. No isomorphism for finite k is asserted. Source: Proposition 5.23, pp. 38–39 (corrected upper-left term on p. 39).

stages.title: The fundamental diagram and elementary comparison cases
stages.description:
Fix the filtered-complex/image-filtration distinction and smallness. Construct the natural square in the strict derived left heart and its difference-map sequence. Establish twist invariance and the proper, affinoid and Stein cases; retain general bicartesianness as Conjecture 6.21.

Targets:

**Filtered cohomology and its image filtration** (construction). For a smooth dagger X/C use the imported analytic cohomology package to set Bⁱ=Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR⁺), Fʳⁱ=Hⁱ(FʳRΓ_dR(X/B_dR⁺)), DRʳⁱ=Hⁱ(RΓ_dR/Fʳ), Filʳⁱ=im(Fʳⁱ→Bⁱ) and Aʳⁱ=ker(Fʳⁱ→Bⁱ). Set Hʳⁱ=Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p(r)) for i≤r and Xʳⁱ=(Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗̂B_st⁺)^{N=0,φ=pʳ}; joint invariants at complex level are derived. Tildes denote left-heart cohomology, ordinary letters its classical part, and bold letters the natural TVS/VS realization when supplied. Filter Bⁱ[1/t] by images of filtered complexes. Fʳⁱ is not identified with Filʳⁱ. Source: §7.1.1 and §§7.2.1–7.2.2, pp. 46–47; Proposition 6.1, pp. 39–40 (import contract).

**Small dagger varieties** (definition). A smooth dagger variety X/C is small when Bⁱ=Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR⁺) is finite free over B_dR⁺ for every i≥0, as in the operational convention of §7.2. The analytic Hyodo–Kato isomorphism then identifies its rank with dim_Fⁿʳ Hⁱ_HK(X) and with dim_C Hⁱ_dR(X). Quasi-compact smooth dagger spaces, naive interiors of quasi-compact spaces, and algebraic analytifications are the source examples; those examples require the corresponding finiteness and base-change inputs, not a definition by quasi-compactness. Source: §7.2, p. 46; §1.2.3 and Remark 1.10, pp. 5–6.

**The fundamental diagram** (construction). For every smooth dagger X/C and 0≤i≤r form the natural commutative square with upper row H̃ʳⁱ→X̃ʳⁱ and lower row F̃ʳⁱ→B̃ⁱ, using the syntomic period map and the map of triangles with common term RΓ_dR/Fʳ. The associated two maps are u=(a,b):H̃ʳⁱ→X̃ʳⁱ⊕F̃ʳⁱ and v=(c,−d):X̃ʳⁱ⊕F̃ʳⁱ→B̃ⁱ. Thus vu=0. X̃ and B̃ are classical. The general assertion that this square is bicartesian is Conjecture 6.21, not an unconditional theorem. Source: §6.4 and Conjecture 6.21, pp. 43–44; equation (6.16), p. 43 (sign convention).

**Twist invariance and the surjectivity reduction** (theorem). For fixed i≥0 the fundamental square is bicartesian for one r≥i iff it is so for every r≥i. Multiplication by t identifies H̃ʳⁱ with H̃ʳ⁺¹ⁱ and F̃ʳ⁺¹ⁱ=tF̃ʳⁱ; the quotient Xʳ⁺¹ⁱ/tXʳⁱ identifies with Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗̂C and the corresponding Bⁱ/tBⁱ with Hⁱ_dR(X), by Hyodo–Kato. For a fixed r, surjectivity of Xʳⁱ⊕Fʳⁱ→Bⁱ in all degrees 0≤i≤r yields the short exact left-heart sequences in that range by induction from degree −1=0. Source: Remark 6.23(ii)–(iii), pp. 44–45.

**Proper analytic comparison over K** (theorem). For a smooth proper rigid analytic X_K/K, with X=X_K×C, all cohomology groups below are finite dimensional and there is a natural B_st-linear G_K-equivariant isomorphism Hⁱ_ét(X,Q_p)⊗B_st≅Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗B_st preserving φ and N. It induces the filtered B_dR comparison with Hⁱ_dR(X_K)⊗_K B_dR. No semistable model is assumed. The induced dual Hom descriptions are strict for the natural weak Hom topologies. Source: Theorem 6.4 and Remark 6.7, pp. 40–41.

**Proper analytic comparison over C** (theorem). For X/C smooth proper rigid analytic and i≥0 there are natural B_st-linear isomorphisms Hⁱ_ét(X,Q_p)⊗B_st≅Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗B_st preserving φ,N and inducing a filtered B_dR isomorphism with Bⁱ⊗_{B_dR⁺}B_dR. The filtration on Bⁱ is im(Hⁱ(FʲRΓ_dR)→Bⁱ). In particular the associated pair (Hⁱ_HK,F⁰(Bⁱ[1/t])) is weakly admissible. This does not identify its lattice with the unfiltered Bⁱ. Source: Theorem 6.8 and Remark 6.13, pp. 41–42 (F⁰ correction).

**The simplified Stein and affinoid diagram** (theorem). For a smooth dagger Stein space or dagger affinoid X/C and r≥0 there is a natural map between strictly exact rows 0→Ωʳ⁻¹(X)/ker d→Hʳ_proét(X,Q_p(r))→Xʳʳ→0 and 0→Ωʳ⁻¹(X)/ker d —d→ Ωʳ(X)^{d=0}→Hʳ_dR(X)→0. The left vertical map is identity, the right is ι_HK⊗θ, and the middle β̃=p⁻ʳβα_r⁻¹. All vertical maps are strict with closed image. Hʳ_proét is Fréchet in the Stein case and LB in the affinoid case; ker β̃≅(Hʳ_HK(X)⊗̂B_st⁺)^{N=0,φ=p^{r−1}}. Set Ω⁻¹=0. Source: Theorem 6.14, p. 43; its cited part-I Corollary 6.9 and Proposition 5.13.

**Bicartesian diagrams for proper, Stein and affinoid spaces** (theorem). The fundamental square is bicartesian for smooth proper X/C and for smooth dagger Stein or affinoid X/C, in all 0≤i≤r by twist invariance. At degree i=r the proper horizontal arrows are injective and Fʳʳ→Filʳʳ is an isomorphism. At degree r in the Stein/affinoid case both horizontal arrows are surjective with common kernel Ωʳ⁻¹/ker d. The latter assertion uses pro-étale cohomology, not étale cohomology of a rigid affinoid completion. Source: Corollaries 6.15 and 6.19, Remark 6.18, pp. 43–44 (pro-étale correction).

stages.title: The qBC filtration and comparison criteria
stages.description:
Identify kernel and cokernel by finite bundle cohomology, construct the canonical qBC filtration and its exact defect sequence, and prove the degreewise and global equivalences with acyclicity, curvature and height. Record noncanonical crystalline and syntomic splittings on a separate branch.

Targets:

**Bundle cohomology measuring the diagram** (construction). For small X, i≥0, r≥0 and n=0,1 put hⁿ_i(r)=Hⁿ(X_FF,E(Hⁱ_HK(X){−r},FilʳHⁱ_dR(X/B_dR))), as a finite BC object. Here {−r} multiplies φ by p⁻ʳ and leaves N fixed, and the lattice is the induced Filʳ lattice in Bⁱ[1/t]. Use hⁿ_{−1}(r)=0. In the range i≤r, or for quasi-compact X with r≥dim X, the tʳ-period isomorphism identifies this modified bundle with the untwisted pair (Hⁱ_HK,F⁰Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR)); the simultaneous change of φ and lattice is essential. Source: §7.2.2 and Lemma 7.7, p. 47; proof of Proposition 7.10, p. 48.

**Kernel and cokernel descriptions** (theorem). For small X and i≤r, h⁰_i(r)≅ker(Xʳⁱ⊕Filʳⁱ→Bⁱ)≅ker(Xʳⁱ→Bⁱ/Filʳⁱ), and h¹_i(r) is the corresponding cokernel. Moreover ker(Hʳⁱ→Xʳⁱ⊕Fʳⁱ)≅h¹_{i−1}(r). These identifications lift to the natural TVS objects, with the difference-map convention of CS.1. Source: Lemma 7.7 and equation (7.6), pp. 46–47.

**The canonical qBC filtration on pro-étale cohomology** (construction). For small X and 0≤i≤r the natural TVS Hʳⁱ is a qBC. Its functorial canonical filtration has successive curvature pieces Hʳⁱ_{>0}≅h¹_{i−1}(r), Hʳⁱ_{=0}≅Aʳⁱ=(Fʳⁱ)_{B_dR⁺-tors}, and Hʳⁱ_{<0}≅h⁰_i(r). The middle piece is a reasonable B_dR⁺-Pair and need not be finite BC. These are associated graded objects, not a canonical direct-sum decomposition. Zero pieces are allowed in every curvature class. Source: Corollary 7.9(i), p. 47, with its proof.

**The exact sequence with two failure terms** (theorem). For small X and 0≤i≤r there is a natural exact sequence of TVS objects 0→h¹_{i−1}(r)→Hʳⁱ→Fʳⁱ⊕Xʳⁱ→Bⁱ→h¹_i(r)→0, with the signs transported from CS.1. Consequently the fundamental diagram in degree i is bicartesian exactly when both h¹_{i−1}(r) and h¹_i(r) vanish. Source: Corollary 7.9(ii), p. 47; Proposition 7.10(a)–(b), p. 48.

**The height formula and its sign** (theorem). For small X and r≥0, ht(Hʳʳ)=dim_Fⁿʳ Hʳ_HK(X)+ht(h¹_{r−1}(r))+ht(h¹_r(r)). Each h¹ term has height ≤0, and height zero occurs only if that term is zero, because it is H¹ of a vector bundle. Therefore ht(Hʳʳ)≤dim_C Hʳ_dR(X), with equality exactly when both failure terms vanish. This strictness is not asserted for every positive-curvature BC: torsion away from ∞ is a counterexample to that broader assertion. Source: Proposition 7.10 proof, p. 48; Remark 3.10, p. 16; Remark 3.8, p. 15.

**The degreewise equivalence of comparison criteria** (theorem). For a small smooth dagger X/C and r≥0 the following are equivalent: the fundamental square at degree i=r is bicartesian; h¹_{r−1}(r)=h¹_r(r)=0; the two pairs (Hʲ_HK(X),F⁰Hʲ_dR(X/B_dR)) for j=r−1,r are acyclic; the TVS Hʳʳ and H_syn^{r+1}(X,r) both have curvature ≤0; ht(Hʳʳ)=dim_C Hʳ_dR(X). The degree r+1 term here is syntomic, not H^{r+1}_proét(X,Q_p(r)); it lies outside the comparison range. Negative-degree pairs vanish. Source: Proposition 7.10 with footnote 21, p. 48.

**The four conjectural properties for a small variety** (theorem). For a small smooth dagger X/C the following families of statements are equivalent: the fundamental squares are bicartesian for all 0≤i≤r; all pairs (Hⁱ_HK,F⁰Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR)) are acyclic; every Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p) has curvature ≤0; ht(Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p))=dim_C Hⁱ_dR(X) for every i. This is an equivalence of properties, not a proof that they hold for every small X. Source: Corollary 7.11 and Remark 7.12, p. 48; Conjectures 7.1, 7.3 and 7.4, p. 46.

**Splitting the crystalline eigenspace complex** (theorem). For a smooth quasi-compact dagger X/C, r≥dim X, and the functorial log-crystalline complex of the analytic package, Hⁱ([RΓ_cris(X)]^{φ=pʳ})≅(Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗B_st⁺)^{N=0,φ=pʳ} as BC objects. The eigenspace complex is quasi-isomorphic to the direct sum of these groups placed in degree i. The splitting depends on cocycle lifts; it is neither canonical nor claimed Galois equivariant. The proof uses the completed unramified coefficient version of HK, with its comparison to the Fⁿʳ version. Source: Lemma 7.13 and Remark 7.14, pp. 48–49.

**A noncanonical decomposition of syntomic cohomology** (theorem). For smooth quasi-compact dagger X/C and r≥dim X, every natural syntomic TVS H_synⁱ(X,r) is isomorphic, noncanonically, to h¹_{i−1}(r)⊕h⁰_i(r)⊕P_i, where P_i is a reasonable B_dR⁺-Pair representing the curvature-zero piece. For i≤r this decomposes pro-étale cohomology through α_r. It does not prove that the canonical qBC filtration splits canonically or that every qBC splits. Source: Proposition 7.15, pp. 49–50.

stages.title: Geometric classes with nonnegative de Rham slopes
stages.description:
Define nonnegative de Rham slopes and prove product closure, algebraic analytification and almost proper cases. Apply the latter to the exact semistable and projective-space tube settings supplied by the geometric owner.

Targets:

**Varieties with nonnegative de Rham slopes** (definition). A smooth dagger X/C has de Rham slopes ≥0 if X is small and, for every i≥0, the filtered module (Hⁱ_HK(X),F⁰Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR)) is acyclic. The term refers to slopes of its modified bundle, not to φ-slopes alone and not to nonnegative Hodge–Tate weights. Source: §8.1, p. 50; Conjecture 7.1, p. 46.

**Nonnegative de Rham slopes for products** (theorem). If smooth dagger X,Y/C have de Rham slopes ≥0, their product has de Rham slopes ≥0. In degree n the cup product gives an injective bundle map ⊕_{i+j=n}E_i(X)⊗E_j(Y)→E_n(X×Y) whose cokernel is coherent and supported at ∞. Equality of the two filtration lattices is not required or asserted. Source: Theorem 8.1(a), p. 50.

**Algebraic analytifications have nonnegative slopes** (theorem). For a smooth finite-type algebraic variety V/C, its dagger analytification Vᵃⁿ has de Rham slopes ≥0. For each i, the algebraic admissible filtered module maps to its analytic counterpart, isomorphically on HK; the resulting bundle injection has coherent cokernel supported at ∞. The analytic lattice may be larger than the algebraic one. Source: Theorem 8.1(b), pp. 50–51.

**Almost proper varieties have nonnegative slopes** (theorem). Let X/C be smooth proper rigid analytic and Z⊆X any closed analytic subvariety. The smooth dagger complement U=X∖Z has de Rham slopes ≥0. No smoothness or normal crossings assumption on Z is imposed in the conclusion. A proper modification reducing the boundary to a simple normal crossings divisor is a proof input. Source: Theorem 8.1(c), p. 51.

**The logarithmic and naive filtration discrepancy** (theorem). With U=X′∖D a resolved almost proper pair and i≤r, the two-term complexes [Hⁱ_ét(U,Q_p(r))→H̃ⁱ_proét(U,Q_p(r))] and [Hⁱ(FʳRΓ_dR(X′ with log D/B_dR⁺))→H̃ⁱ(FʳRΓ_dR(U/B_dR⁺))] are naturally isomorphic in the derived/left-heart realization. These are complexes with maps; no equality of ordinary quotient vector spaces without strictness is inferred. Source: Remark 8.2, p. 51.

**Comparison for semistable tube complements** (application). Let 𝔛/O_K be weak formal with local étale charts Spf(O_K{T₁,…,T_n}/(T₁⋯T_s−π)), 1≤s≤m≤n. Let 𝔝 be locally either ⋂_{j=s+1}^mV(T_j) or ⋃_{j=s+1}^mV(T_j), with the stated compatible charts, and assume 𝔛_K smooth proper. For U=]𝔛_k∖𝔝_k[_𝔛, the base change U_C has de Rham slopes ≥0 and hence bicartesian fundamental diagrams. The comparison RΓ_dR(𝔛_K∖𝔝_K)→RΓ_dR(U) is a filtered quasi-isomorphism; compatible HK and B_dR comparisons transfer the filtered pairs. Source: Proposition 8.3 and the following example, pp. 51–52.

**Small tubular neighbourhoods in projective space** (application). Let X=Pⁿ_K and let Z=Z₁×_X⋯×_XZ_c be a smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersection of c hypersurfaces in the codimension-c setting of Proposition 8.4. There is ε₀∈|K×| such that for positive ε∈|K×| with ε<ε₀, removing the specified tubular neighbourhood Z(ε) instead of Z induces compatible quasi-isomorphisms in de Rham and HK cohomology. The same comparison holds for the union of the Z_j by analytic Čech descent under the source’s complete-intersection hypotheses. The resulting dagger complement over C has de Rham slopes ≥0. The chosen tube definition and its radius inequalities must be part of the geometric supplier. Source: Proposition 8.4 and the following paragraph, p. 52.

stages.title: Inverse limits and proper times Stein
stages.description:
Keep the countable exhaustion as data and compute Milnor/R¹lim obstructions. Prove proper-factor étale Künneth, the required proper-times-Stein limit vanishing and its pro-étale Künneth consequence, then obtain the global bicartesian square without assuming smallness.

Targets:

**Cohomology along a countable exhaustion** (construction). Fix a smooth dagger X/C with a chosen increasing admissible exhaustion X=⋃_{n∈N}X_n by quasi-compact open dagger subspaces, each having nonnegative de Rham slopes. For fixed r use the inverse systems H_n^{r,i},X_n^{r,i},F_n^{r,i},B_n^i,A_n^{r,i} and F̄_n^{r,i}=F_n^{r,i}/A_n^{r,i}=Fil_n^{r,i}, with restriction maps. The global versions are cohomology of the respective derived inverse-limit complexes, not definitions as ordinary limits of groups. In this setting X^{r,i}≅lim X_n^{r,i}, B^i≅lim B_n^i, and R¹lim X_n^{r,i}=R¹lim F̄_n^{r,i}=0. Source: §8.2.1, notation (8.5)–(8.8) and Remark 8.9(i)–(ii), pp. 52–53.

**The inverse-limit obstruction sequence** (theorem). For the chosen exhaustion and a fixed r, in each degree i≤r the Milnor sequences are 0→R¹lim F_n^{r,i−1}→F^{r,i}→lim F_n^{r,i}→0 and 0→R¹lim H_n^{r,i−1}→H^{r,i}→lim H_n^{r,i}→0. The stagewise comparison sequences give 0→lim H_n^{r,i}→lim X_n^{r,i}⊕lim F_n^{r,i}→lim B_n^i→R¹lim H_n^{r,i}→R¹lim F_n^{r,i}→0. If R¹lim H_n^{r,j}=0 in the adjacent degrees needed for all 0≤i≤r, the global sequence 0→H^{r,i}→X^{r,i}⊕F^{r,i}→B^i→0 is exact and R¹lim F_n^{r,i}=0 in that range. Source: Remark 8.9(ii)–(iii), p. 53.

**A de Rham criterion for R¹lim vanishing** (theorem). For the exhaustion above, fixed r and i≤r, R¹lim DR_n^{r,i−1}=0 implies R¹lim A_n^{r,i}=0, which implies R¹lim H_n^{r,i}=0. Here DR_n^{r,j}=Hʲ(RΓ_dR(X_n/B_dR⁺)/Fʳ). Moreover R¹lim(H_n^{r,i}/A_n^{r,i})=0 without the first hypothesis: these quotients lift functorially to finite BC objects. Source: Lemma 8.10, Remark 8.11 and footnote 22, p. 53; Remark 3.15, p. 17.

**Étale Künneth with a proper factor** (theorem). For smooth rigid analytic Y,T/C with Y proper, cup product gives ⊕_{j≥0}Hʲ_ét(Y,Q_p)⊗_{Q_p}H^{i−j}_ét(T,Q_p)≅Hⁱ_ét(Y×T,Q_p) for every i≥0. The sum is finite in each degree. At integral level the corresponding comparison uses a derived tensor over Z_p. The perfect coefficient complex in the projection formula is RΓ_ét(Y,Z_p); no perfection of RΓ_ét(T,Z_p) is assumed. Source: Lemma 8.13, equations (8.14)–(8.15), p. 54 (perfect-factor correction).

**R¹lim vanishing for proper times Stein** (theorem). Let Y/C be smooth proper and S/C smooth dagger Stein, with a strictly increasing admissible covering by open dagger affinoids S_n. Put X_n=Y×S_n. For every i≥0, R¹lim_n Hⁱ_proét(X_n,Q_p)=0. Consequently Hⁱ_proét(Y×S,Q_p)≅lim_n Hⁱ_proét(X_n,Q_p), with the natural cohomological topologies. Source: Proposition 8.12 and Remark 8.16(i), p. 54.

**Pro-étale Künneth for proper times Stein** (theorem). For the same Y,S, cup product gives ⊕_jHʲ_proét(Y,Q_p)⊗_{Q_p}H^{i−j}_proét(S,Q_p)≅Hⁱ_proét(Y×S,Q_p). The tensor products are ordinary tensors with the finite-dimensional proper-factor groups, carrying their natural finite direct-sum topology. This statement is restricted to a proper factor; the analogous algebraic tensor formula fails for the product of two open one-dimensional balls. Source: Remark 8.16(ii), p. 54.

**The fundamental diagram for proper times Stein** (theorem). For smooth proper Y/C and smooth dagger Stein S/C, X=Y×S has a bicartesian fundamental square in LH(C_Q_p) for every 0≤i≤r, r≥0. Its associated sequence is 0→Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p(r))→(Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗̂B_st⁺)^{N=0,φ=pʳ}⊕Hⁱ(FʳRΓ_dR(X/B_dR⁺))→Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR⁺)→0, with the difference-map signs. Smallness of the global space X is not required. Source: Proposition 8.17, p. 55.

stages.title: Arithmetic and geometric period recovery
stages.description:
Remove arithmetic differential and torsion kernels before applying the imported period functors. Prove Theorem 9.3 with Galois and filtration data, and Theorem 9.8 with natural Topological Vector Space Hom and extended modules; retain positive crystalline affinoid bounds and the precise limits of recovery.

Targets:

**Vanishing on the differential error term** (theorem). For a smooth dagger affinoid X/K and i≥1, both Hom^{sm}_{G_K}((Ω^{i−1}(X)/ker d)⊗̂_K C,B_st) and Hom_{G_K}((Ω^{i−1}(X)/ker d)⊗̂_K C,B_dR) vanish. The maps are continuous Q_p-linear; the smooth Hom means the union of Hom_{G_L} over finite L/K. The same argument applies to the relevant Čech terms used for quasi-compact X. For i=0 the differential term is zero. Source: Lemma 9.5 and its proof, pp. 55–56.

**Vanishing on the arithmetic torsion kernel** (theorem). For a small smooth dagger X/K whose base change to C has nonnegative de Rham slopes, set A^{r,i}=ker(Hⁱ(FʳRΓ_dR(X_C/B_dR⁺))→Hⁱ_dR(X_C/B_dR⁺)), i≤r. Then Hom^{sm}_{G_K}(A^{r,i},B_st)=Hom_{G_K}(A^{r,i},B_dR)=0. The topology and G_K action are the natural ones. The quasi-compact proof extends to the other small cases through the finite-free cohomology and strict Čech presentations used in §9.1.3. Source: Lemma 9.6 and §§9.1.2–9.1.3, pp. 56–57.

**Arithmetic pro-étale-to-de Rham recovery** (theorem). Let X/K be smooth dagger and assume X_C has de Rham slopes ≥0 (hence is small). For every i≥0, naturally and strictly for the weak Hom topologies, Hom^{sm}_{G_K}(Hⁱ_proét(X_C,Q_p),B_st)≅Hⁱ_HK(X_C)^∨ as (φ,N,G_K)-modules over Fⁿʳ, and Hom_{G_K}(Hⁱ_proét(X_C,Q_p),B_dR)≅Hⁱ_dR(X/K)^∨ as filtered K-modules. Filtration on Hom is pointwise image in tʲB_dR⁺; smooth invariants are the colimit over finite extensions. These are contravariant duals; the Hodge filtration is retained only with the arithmetic G_K structure. Source: Theorem 9.3; Remark 9.2; §§9.1.1–9.1.3, pp. 55–57.

**Geometric pro-étale-to-period-module recovery** (theorem). Let X/C be smooth dagger with de Rham slopes ≥0. With 𝐇 the natural Topological Vector Space functor of Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p), M=Hⁱ_HK(X) and B=Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR⁺), there are natural B_st- and B_dR-linear isomorphisms Hom_TVS(𝐇,𝐁_st)≅Hom_{Fⁿʳ}(M,B_st) and Hom_TVS(𝐇,𝐁_dR)≅Hom_{B_dR⁺}(B,B_dR). Here Hom_TVS consists of natural transformations between functors on sympathetic algebras valued in LH(C_Q_p), with the boundedness condition of Definition 4.1. It is not the set of arbitrary continuous maps on C-points. These recover extended period modules; no φ,N or Hodge filtration is claimed to be recovered from the geometric functor alone. Source: Theorem 9.8 and §9.2 proof, pp. 57–58 (TVS category correction).

**Positive crystalline recovery for affinoids** (theorem). For a smooth dagger affinoid X/C in degree i, put M=Hⁱ_HK(X), B=Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR⁺) and r=i. Monodromy untwisting identifies X_st^i(M) with X_cris^i(M). The intended strengthened affinoid comparison is Hom_TVS(Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p(i)),B_cris⁺)≅Hom_TVS(X_cris^i(M),B_cris⁺)=M^∨⊗B_cris⁺. After the stated completed unramified scalar extension and duality it recovers φ on M⊗_{Fⁿʳ}F̂ⁿʳ. Also Fil^{i+k}B=t^kB for k≥0. The equality with positive crystalline coefficients is an exact target of Remark 9.9(ii), subject to G-CRIS; the weaker sandwich M^∨⊗B_cris⁺⊆Hom_VS(X_cris^i(M),B_cris⁺)⊆M^∨⊗t^{−i}B_cris⁺ alone does not prove that equality. Source: Remarks 5.19 and 5.21, pp. 38–39; Remark 9.9(ii), p. 58.

**Information and scope of the recovery theorems** (application). For a smooth proper X/C the natural Topological Vector Space functor of Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p) is the constant finite-dimensional Q_p functor. Its geometric period Hom functors therefore retain its rank and the corresponding free extended period modules, while the source’s extra φ,N and filtration data require additional structure. The full recovery assertions for arbitrary smooth dagger spaces, including the sheafified direction of Remark 9.9(iii), are research problems, not theorem targets discharged by Theorems 9.3 or 9.8. Source: Remark 9.9(i),(iii), p. 58; Conjectures 1.6, 1.8 and 9.1, pp. 3–4,55.

sources.title: On the cohomology of p-adic analytic spaces, II: The C_st-conjecture
sources.edition: Author manuscript CN5, compiled 24 November 2024; source of Duke Mathematical Journal 174 (2025), 2203–2301. All page locators use the 61-page author manuscript, not journal pagination.
readSections: §1, pp. 1–8, for theorem scope and conjectures; §5, pp. 31–39, filtered modules and period Hom; §§6–9, pp. 39–58, diagrams, qBC filtration, geometric cases, limits and recovery; Appendix A, pp. 58–60, with the reviewed L0 qualification. Definitions 4.1–4.5 and the reasonable-Pair/filtration arguments in §4.3–4.4 were also read to fix the functor category; the §2–4 inputs are imported by their named owner contracts, not re-proved here.
